newsitem.title: USA: AT&T views FCC ruling as good compromise.
newsitem.headline: AT&T views FCC ruling as good compromise.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Wednesday said it viewed a Federal Communications Commission ruling that reduced local access charges paid by long-distance providers as "a good compromise."

"Today's action is a significant first step -- but only a first step -- in what we expect will be an ongoing process to reduce the inflated access fees we pay to the monopoly local telephone companies," said Robert Allen, chairman and chief executive of AT&T.
Earlier this week the company said it planned to reduce long-distance rates based on the expected FCC action.
Allen said AT&T customers on its basic rate schedule could expect reductions of five percent on daytime calls, five percent on evening calls and 15 percent during the night/weekend period.

Earlier Wednesday, the FCC adopted a sweeping overhaul of the system of telephone charges in order to foster greater competition among the regional phone companies and the long-distance service providers.

Among the new rules, the FCC approved an upfront reduction of $1.7 billion in annual long-distance access charges, which currently total $23 billion. It also approved a total reduction of $18.5 billion over the next five years.
